caveats: All tested encoders are lossy; this audit does not assert perceptual transparency.
All outputs decoded successfully; duration padding is measured and would need explicit trimming/metadata in runtime.
Decode timings are native FFmpeg on desktop, include output resampling to 11025 Hz, and do not predict a Java CLDC decoder or phone MMAPI speed.
Whole-clip PCM sizes are not streaming requirements. A runtime must stream or bound buffers.
Custom Opus packet-bank estimates exclude global lookup tables, implementation and ZIP directory; they are not a J2ME implementation.
Native availability of any compressed codec must be checked on target phones.
Speex validation explicitly uses libspeex. FFmpeg7.1.5 built-in speex decoder doubled the decoded length of a tested 16kHz clip; libspeex decoded its duration correctly.

Opus OPB1 packet-stream Deflate measurements include a 28-byte per-clip descriptor and 16-bit per-packet lengths, preserving source sample count, preskip, gain, granule and packets; global name/ID index, JAR entry overhead and runtime decoder are excluded.
Opus coded bandwidth and SILK/hybrid/CELT mode were parsed from every baseline8kbps12kHz packet TOC on all327 unique clips; input sample rate alone is not the coded audio bandwidth.
